Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings ('target spots') on older, lower leaves, often surrounded by a yellow halo.
treatment: Remove and destroy affected lower leaves; do not compost them.
Apply a protectant fungicide such as chlorothalonil or mancozeb at label rates, repeating every 7-10 days in wet weather.
Mulch around the base to stop soil splash carrying spores onto leaves.
Water at the soil line early in the day so foliage stays dry.
prevention: Rotate tomatoes with non-solanaceous crops for 2-3 seasons.
Space plants for airflow and stake them off the ground.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large greasy grey-green to brown blotches on leaves, often with white fuzzy growth on the underside in humid conditions. Spreads very fast.
treatment: Act immediately - this disease can destroy a crop in days.
Remove and destroy infected plants entirely; do not leave debris in the field.
Apply a fungicide containing mancozeb, chlorothalonil, or copper as a protectant on remaining plants.
Avoid overhead irrigation until the outbreak is controlled.
prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed and transplants.
Monitor closely during cool, wet, humid spells.
Destroy volunteer tomato and potato plants nearby.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown-black with yellow halos; raised scabby spots on fruit.
treatment: Fungicides do not cure bacterial disease - use copper-based sprays to slow spread.
Remove severely infected plants to reduce inoculum.
Stop working among plants while foliage is wet, which spreads bacteria by contact.
Sanitise tools and stakes between plants.
prevention: Use pathogen-free seed; hot-water treat seed if saving your own.
Rotate away from tomato and pepper for at least one year.
Avoid overhead watering entirely where possible.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: No disease symptoms detected. Leaf shows uniform green colouration.
treatment: Continue routine monitoring, especially on lower leaves after rain.
prevention: Maintain balanced fertilisation and consistent watering.
Keep inspecting weekly - early detection is what keeps a crop healthy.

Other___not_tomato.pathogen: Outside the scope of this system
Other___not_tomato.symptoms: This image does not appear to be a tomato leaf. The detection model is trained on four tomato leaf conditions only, so it cannot diagnose other crops.
treatment: Upload a close-up photograph of a single tomato leaf against a plain background.
For other crops, consult a local agricultural extension officer or a crop-specific diagnostic service.
prevention: Photograph one leaf at a time, filling most of the frame.
Use even daylight and avoid shadows or busy backgrounds.
